title: The Count of Monte Cristo
policy: One distinct generated image per cover, character, item, location, lore and faction slot. Retain six functional historical maps.
style: Historically grounded nineteenth-century literary illustration in ink and watercolor on textured paper; coherent restrained palette; no lettering or watermark.

slots.name: The Count of Monte Cristo
slots.description: Alexandre Dumas’s vast adventure of Edmond Dantès, a Marseille sailor erased by conspiracy and remade by imprisonment, education, and treasure. Returning as the Count of Monte Cristo, he enters the lives of his betrayers and their children, only to discover that reward and revenge cannot be controlled with equal certainty.

slots.name: Edmond Dantès
slots.description: A young sailor of the Pharaon, newly given command on his captain's death and about to be married.

slots.name: Mercédès
slots.description: A Catalan girl of the village above Marseille, betrothed to Edmond and courted by her cousin Fernand.

slots.name: Fernand
slots.description: A Catalan fisherman, cousin to Mercédès and in love with her, who makes no secret of his jealousy of Edmond.

slots.name: Danglars
slots.description: The Pharaon's supercargo, careful with figures and quick to resent a younger man promoted over him.

slots.name: Gaspard Caderousse
slots.description: A tailor and neighbour on the Allées de Meilhan, fond of his drink and easily led by cleverer men.

slots.name: Louis Dantès
slots.description: Edmond's father, proud and poor, keeping a small room in Marseille on very little.

slots.name: Pierre Morrel
slots.description: The honourable shipowner of the Pharaon, who judges his men by their work and stands by them.

slots.name: Gérard de Villefort
slots.description: The deputy crown prosecutor of Marseille: ambitious, newly betrothed, and careful never to be associated with his father's politics.

slots.name: Renée de Saint-Méran
slots.description: Villefort's betrothed at the time of his appointment, born into a powerful royalist family.

slots.name: Noirtier de Villefort
slots.description: Villefort's father, a Bonapartist of the old stamp whose politics are a standing danger to his son's career.

slots.name: Abbé Faria
slots.description: An Italian scholar-prisoner who educates Dantès, reconstructs the conspiracy, and bequeaths the Spada secret.

slots.name: Jacopo
slots.description: A smuggler who saves Dantès after his escape and earns his lasting trust.

slots.name: Franz d’Épinay
slots.description: A young French traveller in Italy, cautious by temperament, who accepts the Count's hospitality without quite trusting it.

slots.name: Albert de Morcerf
slots.description: The honourable but sheltered son of Mercédès and Fernand, drawn into the Count’s circle at Rome.

slots.name: Luigi Vampa
slots.description: A brilliant Roman bandit chief bound to Monte Cristo by respect and obligation.

slots.name: Peppino
slots.description: One of Vampa’s men, rescued from execution through the Count’s intervention.

slots.name: Bertuccio
slots.description: The Count's Corsican steward, carrying a vendetta he has never settled and a past he does not discuss.

slots.name: Maximilien Morrel
slots.description: Morrel's son, a captain of Spahis: straightforward, courageous, and plainly his father's child.

slots.name: Julie Morrel
slots.description: Morrel's daughter, chosen to deliver the red silk purse that saves her family.

slots.name: Emmanuel
slots.description: A clerk of the Morrel house, devoted to the family and to Julie.

slots.name: Valentine de Villefort
slots.description: Villefort’s gentle daughter, protected by Noirtier and loved by Maximilien amid a lethal inheritance struggle.

slots.name: Héloïse de Villefort
slots.description: Villefort's second wife, devoted to her son Édouard and closely interested in the family's settlements.

slots.name: Édouard de Villefort
slots.description: The young son whom Héloïse seeks to enrich and whose fate exposes the cost of indiscriminate vengeance.

slots.name: Haydée
slots.description: A young Greek woman of the Count's household, brought out of slavery by him and carrying the memory of a ruined family.

slots.name: Hermine Danglars
slots.description: The Baroness Danglars, formerly linked to Villefort, balancing society, speculation, and an old hidden grief.

slots.name: Eugénie Danglars
slots.description: A gifted pianist with no appetite for the marriage her father is arranging for her.

slots.name: Lucien Debray
slots.description: A ministerial secretary whose political information and affair with Hermine feed profitable speculation.

slots.name: Beauchamp
slots.description: A journalist and Albert’s friend who verifies the Yanina accusation with professional care.

slots.name: Château-Renaud
slots.description: An aristocratic friend of Albert and Maximilien, saved by the latter in North Africa.

slots.name: Benedetto
slots.description: A young criminal raised in Rogliano by Bertuccio's sister-in-law, violent and ungrateful from boyhood.

slots.name: Major Cavalcanti
slots.description: A paid impostor cast as Andrea’s aristocratic father in the Count’s social trap.

slots.name: Louise d’Armilly
slots.description: Eugénie’s music teacher, companion, and partner in flight from Parisian marriage expectations.

slots.name: Barrois
slots.description: Noirtier’s devoted servant and the accidental victim of poison intended for his master.

slots.name: Doctor d’Avrigny
slots.description: The Villefort family physician who recognizes a pattern of poisoning before the household will face it.

slots.name: Marquise de Saint-Méran
slots.description: Renée's mother, royalist to the bone and watchful of her family's standing.

slots.name: Ali
slots.description: Monte Cristo’s mute Nubian attendant, skilled, observant, and utterly trusted.

slots.name: Baptistin
slots.description: The French steward who manages the Count’s Paris household with disciplined discretion.

slots.name: La Carconte
slots.description: Caderousse’s ailing wife, whose suspicion and greed sharpen the danger surrounding the diamond.

slots.name: Ali Pasha of Yanina
slots.description: Haydée’s father, betrayed while relying on Fernand’s military service.

slots.name: Napoleon Bonaparte
slots.description: The exiled emperor whose brief return makes Captain Leclère’s letter politically explosive.

slots.name: Louis XVIII
slots.description: The restored Bourbon king whose government Villefort serves during the Hundred Days crisis.

slots.name: Bonapartist Letter
slots.description: Captain Leclère’s letter from Elba to Noirtier, innocent cargo that becomes the pretext for Dantès’s imprisonment.

slots.name: Faria’s Spada Manuscript
slots.description: The heat-revealed fragment that identifies the treasure concealed on Monte Cristo.

slots.name: Spada Treasure
slots.description: Gold, coin, ingots, diamonds, pearls, and jewels accumulated in the hidden cave.

slots.name: The Abbé’s Diamond
slots.description: A valuable stone Busoni gives Caderousse as a test and belated share of providence.

slots.name: Red Silk Purse
slots.description: The purse once used to aid Louis Dantès, returned full of money and redeemed bills to save Morrel.

slots.name: Model of the Pharaon
slots.description: A miniature announcing that Morrel’s lost ship has been replaced by a new vessel.

slots.name: Emerald Pill Box
slots.description: The Count’s jeweled container for medicines potent enough to heal or kill.

slots.name: Brucine Mixture
slots.description: A carefully measured poison and antidotal regimen at the heart of the Villefort household danger.

slots.name: Noirtier’s Will
slots.description: A legal instrument used to resist Valentine’s unwanted marriage without speech.

slots.name: False Telegraph Dispatch
slots.description: The altered signal that fabricates political news and destroys one of Danglars’s speculations.

slots.name: Yanina Sale Document
slots.description: The authenticated record naming Fernand as the man who sold Haydée and her mother.

slots.name: Poisoned Lemonade
slots.description: The drink consumed by Barrois after poison meant for Noirtier is placed in the household.

slots.name: Duelling Pistols
slots.description: Weapons prepared for the meeting between Albert and Monte Cristo before Mercédès intervenes.

slots.name: Danglars–Cavalcanti Marriage Contract
slots.description: The agreement that collapses when officers arrive for Andrea during the signing.

slots.name: Five-Million-Franc Drafts
slots.description: Danglars’s final liquid fortune, drawn from the Roman firm of Thomson & French.

slots.name: Sleeping Draught
slots.description: The medicine by which Valentine’s apparent death is staged and concealed.

slots.name: Letter to Maximilien
slots.description: The final written direction that carries the lesson to wait and hope.

slots.name: Marseille
slots.description: France’s Mediterranean port and the novel’s point of departure and return.

slots.name: Paris
slots.description: The capital where restored fortunes, old crimes, and a new generation converge.

slots.name: Rome
slots.description: The carnival city in which the mysterious Count first enters Albert and Franz’s lives.

slots.name: Monte Cristo
slots.description: The rocky island that conceals the Spada fortune and gives Dantès his new title.

slots.name: Elba
slots.description: Napoleon’s place of exile, where the Pharaon makes the politically dangerous stop that ensnares Dantès.

slots.name: Leghorn
slots.description: The Tuscan port used by smugglers and by Dantès while converting treasure into power.

slots.name: Nîmes and the Pont du Gard
slots.description: The region where Caderousse keeps an inn and Bertuccio’s Corsican history begins.

slots.name: Yanina
slots.description: Ali Pasha’s court, remembered through Haydée’s testimony and Morcerf’s concealed betrayal.

slots.name: Constantinople
slots.description: The imperial market through which Haydée passes before Monte Cristo purchases her freedom.

slots.name: Old Port
slots.description: The crowded basin into which the Pharaon returns under Dantès’s command.

slots.name: The Pharaon
slots.description: Morrel & Son’s merchant ship, carrying both honest cargo and the fatal letter from Elba.

slots.name: Morrel & Son
slots.description: The shipowner’s counting-house on the Marseille quay.

slots.name: Dantès’s Lodging
slots.description: The modest upper room where Edmond finds his father weakened by hunger.

slots.name: The Catalans
slots.description: The coastal settlement where Mercédès lives among her community and Fernand presses his suit.

slots.name: La Réserve
slots.description: The waterside inn that hosts the betrothal feast and Dantès’s public arrest.

slots.name: Palais de Justice
slots.description: Villefort’s office, where a routine examination becomes a secret political burial.

slots.name: Château d’If
slots.description: The offshore fortress to which Dantès is carried at night.

slots.name: Landing Stair
slots.description: The guarded approach from boat to fortress.

slots.name: Dantès’s Cell
slots.description: The numbered dungeon where despair gives way to the sound of Faria’s digging.

slots.name: Faria’s Cell
slots.description: The abbé’s chamber, schoolroom, workshop, and starting point of the tunnel.

slots.name: The Tunnel
slots.description: The hidden passage joining two prisoners and transforming both their lives.

slots.name: Ramparts
slots.description: The upper walls from which the prison burial sack is thrown into the sea.

slots.name: The Prisoners’ Cemetery
slots.description: The sea itself, used by the jailers as the fortress cemetery.

slots.name: Landing Cove
slots.description: The inlet where the smugglers anchor and Dantès contrives to remain alone.

slots.name: Goat Path
slots.description: The steep route across the island used to conceal Dantès’s purposeful search.

slots.name: Spada Treasure Cave
slots.description: The sealed chamber containing gold, coin, jewels, and the material basis of the Count’s power.

slots.name: Sinbad’s Grotto
slots.description: The transformed underground salon where Franz receives dreamlike hospitality.

slots.name: Hotel de Londres
slots.description: Franz and Albert’s lodging during carnival and their first formal meeting with Monte Cristo.

slots.name: Colosseum
slots.description: The moonlit ruin where Franz overhears Monte Cristo arranging a bandit’s pardon.

slots.name: Piazza del Popolo
slots.description: The public square prepared for executions before the carnival begins.

slots.name: Teatro Argentina
slots.description: The opera house where Franz recognizes the mysterious island host.

slots.name: Palazzo Rospoli
slots.description: The Count’s carnival windows overlooking the Corso.

slots.name: Catacombs of Saint Sebastian
slots.description: Luigi Vampa’s subterranean refuge and the prison from which Albert is rescued.

slots.name: Appian Way
slots.description: The tomb-lined road leading from Rome toward Vampa’s hidden country.

slots.name: Monte Cristo’s House, Champs-Élysées
slots.description: The Count’s meticulously arranged Paris residence, built for hospitality, surveillance, and control.

slots.name: House at Auteuil
slots.description: The suburban house whose garden and red chamber preserve evidence of Villefort’s buried past.

slots.name: Morcerf Residence, Rue du Helder
slots.description: The fashionable household in which Mercédès recognizes Edmond beneath the Count’s appearance.

slots.name: Danglars Residence
slots.description: The banker’s social household, where money, marriage, and concealed affairs intersect.

slots.name: Danglars’s Bank
slots.description: The financial office whose unlimited credit and final drafts become instruments of revenge.

slots.name: Villefort Residence
slots.description: The divided household of prosecutor, poisoner, grandfather, lovers, and endangered heirs.

slots.name: Noirtier’s Chamber
slots.description: A quiet room where an immobilized man communicates through his eyes and defeats a marriage contract.

slots.name: Villefort Garden
slots.description: The wall and lucerne patch across which Valentine and Maximilien conduct their hidden courtship.

slots.name: Paris Opera
slots.description: A glittering public interior where alliances and recognitions cross between private boxes.

slots.name: Montlhéry Telegraph Station
slots.description: The optical telegraph post whose operator is bribed into sending a false signal.

slots.name: Père-Lachaise Cemetery
slots.description: The cemetery where Maximilien’s grief is redirected toward a final test of hope.

slots.name: Court of Assizes
slots.description: The courtroom where Andrea abandons disguise and publicly names his father.

slots.name: Beauchamp’s Newspaper Office
slots.description: The editorial office where evidence about Yanina is verified rather than merely repeated.

slots.name: Morrel Family Home
slots.description: The grateful Marseille family’s Paris household and Maximilien’s emotional refuge.

slots.name: Bell and Bottle Tavern
slots.description: A roadside tavern on the route toward Belgium where Andrea’s flight from Paris finally ends.

slots.name: Charenton Asylum
slots.description: The institution to which the shattered Villefort is taken after the ruin of his household.

slots.name: Text and Illustration Edition
slots.description: The manuscript contains the complete narrative text of Project Gutenberg eBook #1184, divided across all 117 chapters and modeled events. Gutenberg packaging, contents, and illustration-only artifacts are excluded. Maps and illustrations are documented separately in this page.

slots.name: The Hundred Days
slots.description: The opening occurs as Napoleon leaves Elba and briefly returns to power in 1815. A letter that might be harmless under one regime becomes dangerous under another, allowing Villefort to convert political volatility into private concealment.

slots.name: Marseille and Mediterranean Commerce
slots.description: The Pharaon belongs to a trading world connecting Smyrna, Trieste, Naples, Elba, Marseille, Livorno, and the wider Mediterranean. Ships carry news, letters, contraband, credit, and transformed identities faster than courts can correct injustice.

slots.name: Ali Pasha of Yanina
slots.description: The Yanina plot draws on the fall of the historical Ali Pasha in 1822, reshaped by the novel into the concealed origin of Fernand’s title and Haydée’s enslavement.

slots.name: Credit and Reputation
slots.description: Danglars’s fortune depends on confidence, privileged information, and the honouring of drafts. The Count attacks reputation as a financial asset rather than stealing money directly.

slots.name: The Optical Telegraph
slots.description: France’s semaphore network carried coded official messages between stations. The Count’s bribe works because a single operator can introduce a false sign into a trusted chain.

slots.name: Poison, Tolerance, and Antidote
slots.description: The novel treats toxicology as knowledge whose moral character depends on dose and purpose. Noirtier’s tolerance, Héloïse’s murders, and Valentine’s simulated death all use variations of the same principle.

slots.name: Providence and Judgment
slots.description: The Count interprets survival and treasure as authorization to reward and punish. Édouard’s death reveals the error in treating consequences as perfectly containable and changes the final movement from vengeance to mercy.

slots.name: Identity as Performance and Proof
slots.description: Aliases can protect the vulnerable or empower criminals, while voice, memory, scars, documents, and testimony recover identity. The novel repeatedly asks which forms of recognition deserve belief.

slots.name: Wait and Hope
slots.description: Waiting first appears as helpless imprisonment and bereavement. By the ending it becomes chosen endurance: time in which knowledge, mercy, and love can alter what seems final.

slots.name: Household of Monte Cristo
slots.description: The multilingual servants, agents, vessels, properties, and aliases through which the Count acts across borders.

slots.name: Morrel Family and Firm
slots.description: A Marseille commercial household held together by honour, work, gratitude, and mutual care.

slots.name: House of Morcerf
slots.description: The title and fortune built around Fernand’s military career, Mercédès’s memory, and Albert’s inherited honour.

slots.name: Danglars Banking House
slots.description: A financial network that converts information, marriage, and public confidence into speculative power.

slots.name: Villefort Household
slots.description: A prosecutor’s family divided by politics, inheritance, hidden paternity, forbidden love, and poison.

slots.name: Luigi Vampa’s Band
slots.description: The disciplined outlaw company controlling roads and catacombs outside Rome.

slots.name: Royalist State and Courts
slots.description: The monarchy, prosecutors, police, peers, and courts through which reputation becomes official judgment.
